key_insight: In-place quantum multiplication and modular inversion achieve O(n^(1+ε)) gate counts for any ε > 0, with zero ancillas except for standard multiplication by a quantum multiplier.
engineering_relevance: These arithmetic primitives could reduce gate and qubit overheads in quantum applications while overwriting inputs directly with outputs.
method: Derive multiplication algorithms from a unified theorem.
Multiply modulo 2^n using an odd classical or quantum multiplier without ancillas.
Extend to standard multiplication with nonzero multipliers and ancilla-free modular inversion modulo 2^n.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical resource bounds and claims the first simultaneous subquadratic gate and sublinear ancilla counts for these in-place operations, rather than empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Asymptotic savings do not establish practical circuit costs; standard multiplication by a quantum multiplier still requires O(log n) ancillas.
paper_title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
